content.overview: Every company must prepare an annual return of its particulars as at the close of the financial year and file it with the Registrar within sixty days after the AGM, or within sixty days after the AGM should have been held with reasons if it was not held. Current penalties for late/non-filing are ₹10,000 plus ₹100 per day of continuing failure, capped at ₹2,00,000 for the company and ₹50,000 for an officer in default; a company secretary in practice who certifies a non-conforming return is liable to ₹2,00,000.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 92 (Annual return). Every company must prepare an annual return containing the particulars specified by the section as they stood at the close of the financial year, including registered office and business, holding/subsidiary/associate particulars, securities and shareholding, indebtedness, members/debenture-holders, promoters/directors/key managerial personnel, meetings and attendance, remuneration, penalties/compounding and prescribed matters. The return must be signed by the company secretary or, where there is none, by a director; the section provides the relevant form and certification requirements, including for listed companies and companies meeting prescribed capital/turnover thresholds. A copy must be filed with the Registrar within sixty days after the AGM, or if no AGM is held, within sixty days from when it should have been held with a statement of reasons. If the company fails to file within the statutory period, it is liable to a penalty of ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day after the first, capped at ₹2,00,000; every officer in default is liable to ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day, capped at ₹50,000. A company secretary in practice who certifies an annual return otherwise than in conformity with the section/rules is liable to a penalty of ₹2,00,000. Non-filing for three continuous financial years may also engage section 164(2). Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Content and as-of date
sections.body: The annual return records the particulars specified by section 92 as they stood at the close of the financial year, including the registered office and business; holding, subsidiary and associate companies; securities/shareholding and indebtedness; members and debenture-holders; promoters, directors and key managerial personnel; meetings and attendance; remuneration; penalties/compounding; and other prescribed matters.

sections.heading: Signing and certification
sections.body: The return must be signed by the company secretary or, where there is no company secretary, by a director. The section and applicable rules prescribe additional certification requirements, including for listed companies and companies meeting prescribed paid-up capital or turnover thresholds. Check the applicable class and current rule before concluding who must certify.

sections.heading: Filing deadline
sections.body: A copy of the annual return must be filed with the Registrar within sixty days from the AGM. If no AGM is held in a year, filing is due within sixty days from the date the AGM should have been held, together with a statement specifying reasons for not holding it.

sections.heading: Penalty for non-filing
sections.body: Under subsection (5), the company is liable to a penalty of ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹2,00,000. Every officer in default is liable to ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹50,000.

sections.heading: Certification contrary to requirements and disqualification cross-reference
sections.body: Under subsection (6), a company secretary in practice who certifies an annual return otherwise than in conformity with section 92 or the applicable rules is liable to a penalty of ₹2,00,000. Failure to file annual returns for three continuous financial years may also engage the disqualification provision in section 164(2), subject to its terms.

examples.title: Annual return
examples.body: Every company must prepare an annual return of the particulars as they stood at the close of the financial year and file it with the Registrar within sixty days of the annual general meeting.

hypotheticals.question: A company does not hold its AGM and does not file its annual return. When is the return due?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 92 requires filing within sixty days from the date the AGM should have been held, together with a statement specifying reasons for not holding it.

hypotheticals.question: A company fails to file its annual return and the default continues. What is the current penalty structure under section 92(5)?
hypotheticals.analysis: The company is liable to ₹10,000 plus ₹100 per day after the first for continuing failure, capped at ₹2,00,000. Every officer in default is liable to ₹10,000 plus ₹100 per day after the first, capped at ₹50,000. A company secretary in practice who certifies a non-conforming return is subject to the separate penalty in subsection (6).

distinctions.title: Annual-return filing and certification
distinctions.left: The company has a duty to prepare and file the annual return within the statutory period.
distinctions.right: The certification requirement depends on the statutory class/threshold and prescribed rules; a non-conforming certificate has a separate penalty.

rows.right: Certification by the prescribed professional where required

misconceptions.trap: Treating the sixty-day deadline as running only from an AGM that was actually held.
misconceptions.correction: If no AGM is held, the deadline runs from when the AGM should have been held and the company must include reasons.

misconceptions.trap: Using the pre-amendment fine/imprisonment penalty instead of the current penalty amounts.
misconceptions.correction: Use the substituted penalty structure in subsection (5) and the separate subsection (6) penalty for a non-conforming certification.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every company secretary in practice certification has the same threshold and form.
misconceptions.correction: Check the company's class, paid-up capital/turnover thresholds and the applicable prescribed rules.
